thesis_summary.thesis: Kimbell Royalty Partners, LP is a Fort Worth-based publicly traded partnership that owns mineral and overriding royalty interests across U.S. oil and gas basins and pays monthly cash distributions to common unitholders. **[Fact]** The partnership elects to be taxed as a corporation for U.S. federal income tax purposes (`10-K_20260226`, Overview). **[Fact]** As an owner of non-cost-bearing interests, KRP receives a share of production revenues net of post-production costs and taxes but does not fund drilling, lease operating expense, or plugging and abandonment (`same 10-K`). **[Fact]** As of February 20, 2026, **93,396,488** common units were outstanding (`same 10-K`). **[Fact]** FY2025 total revenues were **$333.8 million**, operating income **$132.8 million**, and net income per common unit **$0.62** (`same 10-K`, consolidated statements). **[Fact]** FY2025 cash distributions paid to common unitholders totaled **$149.4 million**, or about **$1.60** per unit (`same 10-K`, cash flow statement).
thesis_summary.why_market_wrong: Yield-oriented investors may treat KRP as a simple bond proxy and miss the embedded acreage option on **~12.3 million gross mineral acres** and **~4.7 million gross ORRI acres**, with more than half of aggregate acreage in the Permian and Mid-Continent. **[Inference]** Screeners that rank on trailing GAAP earnings rather than cash distributions understate owner yield because depreciation and acquisition accounting suppress net income per unit relative to cash paid. **[Inference]** The partnership's **$441.5 million** revolver balance and Apollo-affiliated preferred equity may be priced as permanent leverage overhang rather than as financing for accretive acquisitions that expand the royalty footprint. **[Inference]** Q1 2026 revenue and earnings softness may be extrapolated as structural when FY2025 production still rose to **25,760 Boe/d** (`10-K_20260226`).
